explain.say: A man who cannot speak watches golfers through a fence and moans whenever someone shouts for a caddie, because it sounds like his lost sister's name. So William Faulkner opens The Sound and the Fury, published in 1929. A gentle note: the novel includes a suicide and the racism of its time and place. The timeline shows the days it is built from.

explain.say: Here is the Compson family of Jefferson, Mississippi, once grand, now decaying. Three brothers each define themselves by their sister Caddy, who never gets a section of her own. Benjy adores her, Quentin is obsessed with her honour, Jason resents her. Dilsey, the family's Black servant, holds the house together. Why might Caddy be the missing centre?

Look at Benjy's day, the seventh of April 1928, which opens the book. Benjy is a disabled man of thirty-three with no sense of time, so a smell or a word throws him decades back without warning. Faulkner marks some jumps with italics. It is confusing on purpose: you feel time the way Benjy does. Can you think of a clue a jump has happened?

explain.say: The book grows clearer as it goes. On the left, Benjy and Quentin, whose sections swirl with memory; Quentin's ends on the day in 1910 he takes his own life at Harvard. On the right, Jason's bitter but readable voice, and a final section told from outside, centred on Dilsey at Easter. Why might Faulkner start with the hardest voice?

The title comes from Macbeth: life is a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing. Faulkner literally begins with a tale told by Benjy. Yet Dilsey, at the Easter service, feels she has seen the beginning and the end. Superb. Challenge: put the four days in the order you would have told them, and say why.

faq.q: Why is the first section of The Sound and the Fury so confusing?
faq.a: It is told by Benjy, a disabled man with no sense of time, whose memories from many years break into the present without warning. Faulkner uses italics to signal some shifts, and readers piece the story together slowly.
The only daughter of the family, loved by Benjy, idealised by Quentin and resented by Jason. Her loss of reputation, failed marriage and exile haunt all three brothers, yet she never narrates.

faq.q: Where does the title The Sound and the Fury come from?
faq.a: From Macbeth's speech after his wife's death, which calls life a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing. The novel opens with Benjy's narration.
asks: The Sound and the Fury Macbeth

faq.a: Quentin, a student at Harvard, tormented by Caddy's disgrace and his obsession with time and honour, drowns himself in the Charles River on 2 June 1910. His section follows that last day.
The Black woman who has served the Compsons for decades and holds the failing family together. The final section, on Easter Sunday 1928, centres on her endurance and faith.
